purpose: The Engineering Assurance release this repository adopts, and the digests of the artifacts it actually reads from that release. Component version pins are NOT restated here: the packaged compatibility matrix is their authority and a second copy would drift from it.
matrix_authority: engineering_assurance/compatibility-matrix.json in the installed distribution. scripts/check_shared_pins.py observes the local toolchain and delegates every verdict to engineering_assurance.compatibility.
registry: Every npm component resolves from the public npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). The internal npm.ix mirror must not appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc, and is not an oracle for whether a release landed. Querying an @agent-ix package needs --@agent-ix:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org; a bare --registry does not override the scoped .npmrc entry.

engineering_assurance.release_form: git tag v0.2.1, a source distribution; the tag is the released artifact

repinned_workflow_component.why: The hosted workflow pinned @agent-ix/quoin@0.22.5, which the packaged compatibility matrix names explicitly incompatible: it 'predates the `quoin change-assurance` surface; seal, intake, and receipt commands do not exist'. Every command this migration's chain runs is on that surface, so the old pin could not have worked. @agent-ix/ix-flow@0.0.4 was absent from the workflow entirely and is now installed.

repinned_ix_flow.why: TL-192 (mirrored from tl-mltl and tl-syntax): the packaged compatibility matrix authoritative for this repository's pin (matrix_authority above) classifies ix-flow strictly at the exact pinned version, so a locally-installed 0.2.3 against a v0.2.0 matrix pinning 0.0.4 classified as unknown, not compatible, and failed the local qualification gate. engineering-assurance v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, agent-ix/engineering-assurance#47) re-pins the matrix to ix-flow 0.2.3 with human acceptance recorded (accepted_by Peter Krenesky, accepted_at 2026-09-10). This repository's engineering_assurance pin above moved from v0.2.0 to v0.2.1 in the same change so the workflow literal and the matrix authority agree; quire-cli and quoin stay at their already-accepted versions.

consumed_artifacts.why: The authority on which component versions are pinned. Deliberately carries no digest here: it is expected to advance as the matrix is re-accepted, and pinning its bytes locally would make this repository a second acceptance authority.

consumed_artifacts_note: This list shrank to one entry when the retained evidence was deleted. verification_semantics.py, schemas/pgm01-compatibility-view-v1.schema.json and the two PGM-01 positive-control fixtures were pinned by digest because the compatibility view read them; that view is gone, so this repository no longer reads them and pinning bytes it does not read would be a claim about work it does not do. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: artifact_digest_mismatches now has nothing with a digest to re-hash and reports an empty list for that reason, not because a comparison passed.

upstream_dependency.why: The compiled pin is an exact commit reachable from the tl-syntax Stage 1 integration branch when admitted; it is not a moving branch head. It is the Stage 1 integration commit reachable from the tl-syntax codex/tl-207-v1-spec branch; the earlier 4a561419 commit was tagged v0.3.0; Cargo.toml pins the current commit by rev, not by tag, so scripts/check_shared_pins.py can cross-check one literal across every file that names it, and the tl-syntax version requirement is =0.3.0 to match. The parser consumes its shared catalog and requirement-context types for the additive context-bound report, its future-operator lowering API for the clean-ascii v2 dialect, and its exported CORPUS_DIR constant to read the shared past-history corpus in place instead of vendoring a copy, while leaving the span-free semantic-identity family unconsumed. The authorship basis does not move: it is the revision whose bytes were read when this dialect was authored, and docs/ATTRIBUTION.md records both facts and the consumed/unconsumed delta separately. This pin field was last synchronized with Cargo.toml at agent-ix/tl-parse#32 (compiled_revision 8dc18eec) and silently drifted two pin bumps behind (#36 to e70f2379, #39 to 842d8255) before agent-ix/tl-parse TL-205/TL-204 caught and closed the gap. scripts/check_shared_pins.py (make pins) already cross-checks this field against Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, fuzz/Cargo.lock and src/lib.rs and would have failed loudly on that drift had it been run against it; TL-205 found the drift by git-history inspection instead.

known_drift: Resolved by the TL-192 bump to v0.2.1: engineering-assurance v0.2.0 packaged compatibility-matrix.json with accepted.state = pending_human_acceptance and shipped no human_acceptance_recorded predicate (agent-ix/engineering-assurance#20). v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, #47) carries accepted.state = accepted with accepted_by and accepted_at populated, so the record this repository now reads is a real release carrying the acceptance rather than a branch head.

Historical: the human acceptance itself was never in doubt: Peter Krenesky accepted the FR-012 matrix on 2026-09-01, attributed on engineering-assurance main as ae50e13, and the pinned release now carries it (see above).
